answer: Persistent activity weighting. Each identity's voting weight is multiplied by a decay factor raised to its idle time, so splitting into many fresh identities yields negligible influence, like grains of sand on a dune. An attacker must keep every fake identity continuously active across the juniper network's task epochs, paying compute and transaction costs that scale linearly with identity count. Below the ocean of legitimate long-lived accounts, the marginal cost per sybil rises faster than any reward it can capture.
